# An epic and its stories

Follow this once the owner has accepted lane L for a request. An epic is one large piece of work cut into two to ten stories; no work is started here. It ends with the epic and every story queued as draft tickets in one pull request.

1. Interview the owner about the whole epic, one question at a time as `./ask.md` says: why this work is wanted, for whom, what the owner forbids (the Vetoes), and what the owner has already settled for every story (the Decisions). These four are open questions; ask each only when the request did not already answer it. An answer that settles a choice for every story is a Decision, never a line of Intent: keep it with the owner's own sentence.
2. Propose the split: two to ten stories. Each has a title in business language, one to five lines of Intent, and the earlier stories it waits for (its `depends_on`). Show the owner the epic title, its Intent lines, its Vetoes, its Decisions and the stories in order, in plain words, and ask for approval as `./ask.md` says. Change the split as the owner asks and show it again. Never add a point the owner did not make.
3. Only on an explicit yes, write the split file outside the working tree, for example in the system temporary folder, in English, as YAML with the keys `title`, `intent`, `vetoes`, `decisions` and `stories`: `intent`, `vetoes` and `decisions` are lists of lines, and each story has a `title`, an `intent` list and `after`, the numbers of the earlier stories it waits for. Write each Decision as `<decision> — "<the owner's sentence>"`, a faithful English translation of the owner's words when they were not in English, with no `D-` number: the command numbers them D-01, D-02 in order. Leave `decisions` out when the owner settled nothing. When config.yml has `people`, follow `./ids.md` for the creator's initials and give no id; with no `people`, or with ids from a tracker, give an `id` on the epic and on every story: the next free one, or the tracker key the owner names.
4. Run `accord new ticket --type epic --lane L --split <file> --queue` as `./similar.md` says: it prints the similar tickets of the epic and of every story and writes nothing until you judge them; run it again with `--related <id>` or `--related none`. On any other exit 2, show the message and stop: nothing was written or pushed. On exit 0 it has pushed one commit holding the epic, with its Decisions numbered and its `## Approach` listing the stories in order, and every story to one backlog branch, and printed the `branch:`, `base:`, `title:` and `merge:` lines and the ticket paths.
5. Run `accord pr <the epic's id>`, which reads the epic from the backlog branch: on exit 2 show its message and stop. Write each section a `remaining:` line names into the body file it printed, from the epic's Intent and the split, and nothing more. Open the pull request when `gh` is available with `gh pr create --head <branch> --base <base> --title "<title>" --body-file <body-file>`, using the `title:` and `body-file:` lines of `accord pr`, not those of step 4; otherwise show the `branch:` line and ask the owner to open it with that title and body. Read the `merge:` line as accord-queue does: `merge: at-once` merges it with `gh pr merge <branch>` and the strategy of `git.merge`; `merge: owner` says the pull request waits for a person.
6. Report the epic id, each story id with the stories it waits for, and the pull request. Say each story is picked up later with `/accord-pickup <id>`, in its own worktree and pull request, in parallel when nothing it waits for is unfinished, and that each story then runs lane M: its own intent interview, approach, plan and review.

## Rules

- The epic itself gets no approach and no plan critique: the owner's yes to the split is its approval; each story its usual critique when it is picked up, and its scout, planner and reviewers read the epic's Vetoes and Decisions by themselves.
- Run the command only after the explicit yes to the split shown in step 2; a changed split needs a new yes.
- Never claim, start or build a story here, never merge with admin rights, and never push by hand: the command pushes.
